lead: you married in at twenty-six, and the promise you made that day put you permanently on a roll you had finished reading before the speeches were over. nobody has ever disputed your place in that house.
sun: a wedding puts the whole population of them in one room, in front of somebody who has just been added to the list. by the end of that afternoon you had the shape of the house: the one bond in it that everything else is set around, the courtesies kept up because they always have been, the brother who was going to go. none of that has needed revising since.
moon: the promise did not come with a term or a get-out, and it did not ask what you had noticed. what you entered that day is judged in decades, and you have kept it to the letter — the hospital runs, the loans, the difficult one phoned on his birthday for twenty-six years. leaving is the one motion it makes no provision for.
pull: the reading was finished in an afternoon and the promise has no end date. you will be at every one of their funerals, correct about all of them, and asked to speak at two.
tension: they bring you the disputes now, and they are right to — twenty-six years without one threat to leave is the whole of your standing there. what you hold was never an opinion; it is what you saw at the reception, and somebody bound in for life cannot say a permanent thing out loud. so they get the smaller answer, gratefully, and the smaller answer is the wrong size every time.
cost: you were right about that house on the day you joined it, and twenty-six years have confirmed every line of it, which is not the usual result of marrying in. the promise obliges you to the whole of them and contains no clause about being right. you will be the last one standing at that graveside, holding what you knew that first afternoon and never said.

lead: nobody in the building has been here as long as you, and the paperwork proves it by nine years. the reading you have of the place was finished long before most of them moved in.
sun: thirty years of a building is thirty years of watching who arrives and who is on the way out, and the sorting got easy a long time ago. within a month of anyone moving in you know whether they are here for a while or here until the next thing, and which of the arrangements the place runs on is real and which is only manners now. none of it comes from asking.
moon: seniority here is arithmetic. you outlasted it into existence — every person who could have overruled you sold up and went, one at a time, until the longest memory in the place belonged to the member who had never been in the middle of it. with nobody above, a reading has nothing to be checked against, and yours has stood for decades on that alone.
pull: the date makes you the most inside person in the building, and thirty years have not once put you inside it. nobody is left who could tell you the reading is wrong.
tension: the newest arrivals are told to knock on your door, and they come up with the good version of themselves ready, because thirty years is the only credential the place recognises. what they meet is somebody who finished placing them on the stairs the week they moved in. the welcome is genuine and the placing is already done, and both are visible, and the word that goes round afterwards is that you are hard to get past.
cost: no reading you have taken in this building has come back wrong — who was going to last, which of them would be trouble, which marriage on the second floor was already over. none of it has been tested. everyone qualified to disagree sold up or died, so the accuracy and the tenure have hardened into a single fact, and what the building trusts is the date.

lead: the funerals still bring you back, and everyone in the room can place you inside a sentence. what the town was actually built on came up in your hands eleven years ago and has not gone back down.
sun: the place is named after what it used to do, and everybody there still describes themselves with it, including you — the surname places you in a second, the whole street knew which house. from off it by a few degrees you could see which of them had actually moved on and which were being kept upright by a thing that shut before they were born. you had that sorted before you left.
moon: sorting stops when the shape is clear. this does not. what shut the place had a reason, and the reason had an arrangement under it, and by the third winter of going through it you had what the shutting was actually about — whose land it was, who was owed, which of them went quiet and got paid. you came out of that. it came up anyway.
pull: they can still name the house you were born in. you went to the bottom of the place you came from, and nothing down there was ever going to tell you when to stop.
tension: at a funeral somebody puts the standard line to you about how it used to be, warmly, expecting the standard line back. what you have is the arrangement that line was built to cover, with names in it and dates. saying it takes the afternoon down and takes your own standing there with it, so you agree instead, and the agreeing reads as the manners of somebody who got out, and that is what goes round the room.
cost: any place with a story about itself will come apart for you at the true joint, and people bring you theirs because the answer is always the real one. the one you did it to first was your own. the town is still there, still able to name you on sight, and what everyone else goes back there for is the thing you pulled up.

lead: every place you turn up to has your name on its list, and no room on that list has ever had all of you in it. doubled, with nothing in you that just belongs.
sun: rooms cannot work out what you are doing there. attendance is perfect — the subs, the birthdays, the shift nobody wanted — and none of it produces what a room reads as ordinary membership, because that comes off people who are not also watching the shape of the evening. so every group you have joined gets round to asking whether you want to be there, and the evidence behind the question is your attendance.
moon: the recall is where it shows. other people remember an evening as having been in it — the warmth, the noise, what it felt like at the table. what comes back to you is a diagram: who had gone quiet by ten, which friendship was over, which of them was the reason it held. no night in your life is stored the other way.
pull: you are on every list and inside none of them. no counterweight anywhere — no room, no hour, no person in front of whom the few degrees close.
tension: just be here is the ask, and it comes from whoever loves you most, at the end of a good evening, in the kindest words available. you were there. you were there for the whole of it, earlier than anybody, and you will be there next time. what they want put down is not a thing you are holding, so nothing gets put down, and what they take from that is the confirmation.
cost: nothing about a group has to be waited out. the shape arrives whole — which pairs are carrying it, which of it will not last the year — and the length of your acquaintance changes nothing about the accuracy. no group in your life has turned out to be other than what you saw at the door. being wrong that way is most of what other people mean by belonging.
